obligation: FSMA Intentional Adulteration (food defense) rule
basis: Part 121 covers facilities required to register under FD&C Act section 415 (21 CFR 121.1). The plant has been a registered food facility since February 2023 because the smoked seafood room makes FDA-regulated food, so the USDA-only exemption in 21 CFR 1.226(g) no longer applies. Not a very small business: human food sales of about $148 million are far above the $10 million base in 121.3. A small business under 121.3 (242 FTE, fewer than 500), whose compliance period ended in 2020. Scope and the 121.5 exemptions are analyzed in P03 section 1

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (proposed)
basis: No final rule. As proposed (226.2(a)), Food and Agriculture has no sector criterion, so coverage depends on exceeding the SBA size standard. The company has 250 employees against the 1,000-employee standard for NAICS 311612 (13 CFR 121.201)

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System rule
basis: Applies by MTSA facility or vessel status (33 CFR 101.605). The inland plant is not on navigable water and holds no Coast Guard facility security plan

obligation: FSIS HACCP systems
basis: Official establishment under a federal grant of inspection (Federal Meat Inspection Act), with HACCP plans for four processing categories. Electronic CCP records fall under 417.5(d)

obligation: FSIS recalls
basis: Same official establishment status; written recall procedure with the 24-hour FSIS notice

obligation: FDA seafood HACCP
basis: The smoked seafood room processes fish under a seafood HACCP plan

obligation: FDA food facility registration and renewal
basis: Registered in February 2023; renewal is due between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31 (1.230(b))

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
basis: The reporting duty falls on the registrant of a food facility (350f(a)(1)). The company is that registrant for the seafood room

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, disposal, breach notice)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents: employee records in the payroll service and online store customer accounts with email and password

obligation: PCI DSS through the acquirer agreement
basis: Card data is handled by the e-commerce vendor's hosted payment page and a vendor-managed encrypting terminal. No card numbers are stored or processed on company systems

obligation: OSHA process safety management
basis: About 16,000 lb of anhydrous ammonia, above the 10,000 lb threshold quantity in Appendix A. The PSM program is owned by the Maintenance and Refrigeration Manager and is not analyzed in P03

obligation: EPA risk management program
basis: Same ammonia quantity, above the 10,000 lb threshold in 40 CFR 68.130. Context for risk and incident response; not analyzed in P03

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT benchmark)
basis: Neither Part 121 nor 9 CFR Part 417 sets technical controls for OT. The plant runs PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, a historian, an MES and a refrigeration controller

obligation: Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards
basis: The statutory authority for CFATS lapsed in July 2023

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules
basis: Privately held LLC with no registered securities

obligation: FAR basic safeguarding and covered telecommunications clauses
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts; no federal government customer in the customer master

obligation: Protected Critical Infrastructure Information program
basis: The company has never submitted information to DHS under the PCII program

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
basis: Policy conditions require use of the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors

obligation: Customer notice of events affecting product safety or supply
basis: Grocery chain and distributor agreements require prompt notice of events affecting product safety, delivery or customer data

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Reaches vendor accuracy claims the company relies on (the AI vision vendor's 99% detection claim)

obligation: Florida Security of Communications Act (recording consent)
basis: The AI vision cameras capture images only; the vendor confirmed they have no microphones

obligation: State AI and employment AI laws (for example Colorado SB26-189)
basis: The company operates only in Florida and its AI uses make no decision about any person
